definitions.explanation: A rendering of text from one language into another. Used as both a standalone noun and as a suffix indicating the language translated into.

examples.japanese: ⟦{英語|えいご}→英語：02274_eigo⟧{訳|やく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}む→読む：00426_yomu⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{小説|しょうせつ}→小説：01434_shousetsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧{訳|やく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}た→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: The Japanese translation of this novel was published.

examples.japanese: ⟦{原文|げんぶん}→原文：20563_genbun⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{訳|やく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{見比|みくら}べてみた。
examples.english: I compared the original text with the translation.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{詩|し}→詩：02139_shi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{訳|やく}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{難|むずか}しい→難しい：00517_muzukashii⟧。

notes:
Read as やく, this is a Sino-Japanese reading of ⟦{訳|わけ}→訳：01095_wake⟧ used specifically in the sense of 'translation'. Not to be confused with ⟦{訳|わけ}→訳：01095_wake⟧ (reason, meaning). Commonly used as a suffix attached to a language name to indicate the target language of a translation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{英|えい}{訳|やく}→英訳：16317_eiyaku⟧: English translation
- ⟦{和|わ}{訳|やく}→和訳：17845_wayaku⟧: Japanese translation (from a foreign language)
- ⟦{直|ちょく}{訳|やく}→直訳：13629_chokuyaku⟧: literal translation
- ⟦{意|い}{訳|やく}→意訳：17846_iyaku⟧: free translation / liberal translation
- {新|しん}{訳|やく}: new translation
- {訳|やく}{者|しゃ}: translator
- {訳|やく}{文|ぶん}: translated text

KANJI READINGS:
- やく: translation (Sino-Japanese reading used in compounds)
- わけ: reason, meaning, circumstances — the native Japanese reading; see separate entry

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{翻訳|ほんやく}→翻訳：01725_honyaku⟧: translation — the full two-kanji word meaning 'translation' (both the act and the result)
- ⟦{通訳|つうやく}→通訳：03516_tsuuyaku⟧: interpretation — oral translation between speakers
